 Kochi Metro becomes first in India to secure co-branding rights for all stations 
 Kochi Metro Rail Ltd is implementing semi-naming rights across its stations to generate additional revenue. This initiative will boost non-ticket revenue to ₹50 crore in the financial year 2026-27. TIMESOFINDIA.COM

 Kochi Metro 1st to co-brand all stations Kochi Metro Rail Ltd ( KMRL ) has become the first Metro network in the country to secure semi-naming rights for all its stations, giving a boost to its non-ticket revenue. Under the initiative, all 25 stations on the Blue line will carry a brand name alongside their existing names. Only 18 stations had semi-naming rights last year. "A central highlight of KMRL's commercial strategy is its semi-naming rights (station branding) model. The process of awarding semi-naming rights for Vyttila Metro Station has entered its final stages. Once finalised (within a month), KMRL will generate 100 per cent branding revenue from all its active stations," a senior KMRL official said. With this, station co-branding will fetch a revenue of ₹6 crore a year. The measure is part of its efforts to achieve a 51.52 per cent growth in non-fare box revenue (NFBR) to reach ₹50 crore in the current financial year (2026-27) as against ₹33 crore in the last FY. Earlier, a major part of the NFBR was the ₹209 crore royalty paid by Axis Bank over 10 years as part of an agreement for the automated fare collection system. However, it (over ₹30 crore a year) ended in FY 2025-26. KMRL registered an operational profit of ₹52.64 crore for FY 2025-26, when the company's net loss came down to ₹352.49 crore from ₹430.5 crore in the previous year. While the original detailed project report prepared during the planning phase projected a daily ridership of 3.8 to 4.2 lakh upon full Phase 1 operational stabilisation, the current average daily ridership is only 1.25 lakh. This has necessitated KMRL to seek maximum NFBR. KMRL managing director G Priyanka instructed the department heads to proactively lay the groundwork for commercial monetisation along the upcoming Phase 2 corridor, which spans from JLN Stadium to Infopark. "Already, five prospective clients have approached us for semi-naming rights. Upon its completion, expected by Aug 2027, KMRL will immediately deploy semi-naming rights for all 11 stations alongside internal and external train advertising, as well as ad placements on pillars and medians," the official added. KMRL has explored new avenues for finding non-operational revenue this year. "We've awarded median beautification along the 15km stretch from Edapally to Tripunithura section. While it will help raise a green space along the medians, we intend to rake in ad revenue through license fees and advertisements. We've awarded the same, for which the license fee comes to ₹30 lakh per annum," he said. The Metro authorities started audio advertisements on trains on an experimental basis. The ads will be aired just before the train reaches the intended station mentioned by the client. Film shooting inside stations and 'Save the Date' reel-making inside metro trains are other NFBR sources. A four-hour film shoot on Tuesday helped it earn ₹1 lakh. "We've also recently tendered the leasing out of optical fiber cables to telecom companies for Wi-Fi internet connection, etc. We're also exploring the possibility of telecom tower lease-out, for which the tenders will be issued soon," the official said. The rental income from property development in stations has increased with clients like IIM-Calicut (a new building at Cusat station) and 'i by Infopark' (a nine-storey building at South Station) coming in. KMRL also has EV charging stations (Muttom, Cusat stations), and rents out space for ATMs, banks (Federal Bank at Aluva station), dormitories (Pathadipalam and MG Road stations), and hotels (Aluva station). Meanwhile, the Bliss City project, a 31.43-acre mixed-use development in Kakkanad, is transitioning to an active construction site. "The initial phase will focus on a unique design integrating commercial, shopping, and entertainment facilities," the official added. Comments
